paragraphs: This paper develops a speech dialogue system that can listen while speaking. Its central problem is deciding when to respond, keep waiting, or interrupt during an ongoing conversation. The system connects a large language model to perception and speech-production modules that operate together, allowing incoming speech to remain relevant while the system is producing an answer.

The language model handles both conversational content and timing decisions through next-token prediction. Alongside ordinary text, it emits control tokens that operate a two-state mechanism called a neural finite state machine. A serialized, real-time representation of the conversation lets the model use the same prediction process to generate answers and coordinate conversational actions.

In automatic evaluations designed to simulate real interactions, the system reduced average response latency by more than threefold relative to LLM-based half-duplex systems. More than half of evaluated interactions received a response within 500 milliseconds. The authors also report 8% higher interruption precision than the best available commercial voice-dialogue LLM, using an eight-billion-parameter model.
neurips-2024-a-full-duplex-speech-dialog.tldr: An LLM coordinates simultaneous listening and speaking through control tokens, improving response latency and interruption precision in evaluated speech interactions.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether language-model alignment should begin during pre-training. The authors call this approach native alignment, distinguishing it from alignment performed later through instruction tuning or reinforcement learning. Their focus is Arabic language models, where they examine how changing the model's initial learning material affects both its capabilities and alignment.

The proposed approach uses extensively aligned pre-training data. Its aim is to prevent unaligned content from being learned from the beginning and to make the resulting pre-trained models more useful. This makes the choice of pre-training material part of the alignment strategy, extending the question beyond how a completed base model should subsequently be adapted.

The study includes experiments and ablations examining model performance and alignment stability. The authors also release open-source Arabic models that achieve reported state-of-the-art results on several benchmarks. These findings support investigating alignment at the pre-training stage; the stated aim of preventing unaligned content should be understood as a design objective, rather than a guarantee established by benchmark performance.
neurips-2024-alignment-at-pre-training-t.tldr: The paper studies alignment through Arabic pre-training data and releases models with reported state-of-the-art benchmark performance.

paragraphs: AROMA models physical systems described by partial differential equations using a compact representation that retains spatial meaning. Its encoder and decoder use local neural fields to represent physical quantities across space. They can handle irregular grids and point clouds, allowing the framework to work with different geometries without first dividing the input into patches.

The resulting latent representation is smooth and arranged as a sequence whose elements can be interpreted spatially. This gives a conditional transformer a structured representation on which to model changes over time. The approach therefore connects flexible spatial encoding with temporal prediction, keeping spatial organization available after the original physical field has been compressed.

AROMA uses a diffusion-based formulation for modeling these dynamics. The authors report greater stability and longer successive predictions than conventional training based on mean squared error. Experiments on one- and two-dimensional equations show superior simulation performance. These results connect the framework's spatial representation and temporal formulation to its ability to reproduce complex dynamics over longer rollouts.
neurips-2024-aroma-preserving-spatial-st.tldr: AROMA combines spatially interpretable local neural fields with diffusion-based temporal modeling to improve PDE simulation stability and rollout length.

paragraphs: This paper asks whether generated images represent cultures competently, beyond looking attractive, realistic, or faithful to a prompt. It proposes evaluating two dimensions: cultural awareness and cultural diversity. Separating them allows the evaluation to examine both models' knowledge of cultural artifacts and the breadth of cultural representations appearing in their outputs.

The authors introduce CUBE, covering eight countries across different cultural regions and three categories: cuisine, landmarks, and art. They combine structured knowledge bases with large language models to assemble the evaluation material. CUBE-1K supplies high-quality prompts for assessing awareness, while the larger CUBE-CSpace dataset provides reference material for assessing diversity. A quality-weighted Vendi score supports the diversity evaluation.

The evaluations reveal substantial cultural-awareness gaps across countries and examine diversity when prompts leave cultural details unspecified. This matters because an underspecified request can expose which cultural representations a model tends to produce. The authors describe their construction method as extendable to additional regions and concepts, offering a route to broader cultural evaluation.
neurips-2024-beyond-aesthetics-cultural-.tldr: CUBE evaluates cultural awareness and diversity in text-to-image models, revealing substantial awareness gaps across the countries studied.

paragraphs: BitDelta investigates how much information must be stored to preserve a language model's fine-tuning changes. It separates a fine-tuned model's weights into the original pre-trained weights and a difference, or delta. The motivating hypothesis is that this additional information may be highly compressible, given that fine-tuning requires much less computation than pre-training.

The method quantizes the delta to one bit while retaining a high-precision base model. Multiple fine-tuned models can therefore share that base and store their individual changes compactly. The one-bit claim concerns the differences introduced by fine-tuning, so the shared base remains an essential part of the representation.

Experiments cover Llama-2, Mistral, and MPT models, including models with up to 70 billion parameters, and report minimal performance degradation across tested settings. In multi-tenant settings, the authors report more than tenfold reductions in GPU memory requirements and per-user generation latency. The findings suggest substantial redundancy in the tested fine-tuning updates and practical benefits when serving many customized models together.
neurips-2024-bitdelta-your-fine-tune-may.tldr: BitDelta compresses fine-tuning differences to one bit, preserving tested performance closely while reducing multi-tenant storage and serving costs.

paragraphs: BLURD addresses a difficulty in evaluating vision models: researchers need controlled changes in images, but controlled synthetic images may differ from real photographs. Rendering offers flexibility over the factors being tested, while collecting controlled real-world images is expensive and less adaptable. This realism gap can complicate the interpretation of a model's responses to visual changes.

The method combines 3D rendering with Stable Diffusion to create datasets containing rendered and photorealistic images with identical factors. This pairing connects the control available through rendering with more photographic-looking outputs. It allows evaluations to compare representations across these image forms while keeping the specified factors aligned.

The authors use this dataset family to obtain deeper insights into representations learned by different CLIP backbones. The contribution is an evaluation method for examining variation, potential shortcuts, biases, and inaccuracies through controlled image generation. By making matched factors available in both rendered and photorealistic forms, BLURD supports a more informative investigation of how image appearance relates to model behavior.
neurips-2024-blurd-benchmarking-and-lear.tldr: BLURD combines 3D rendering and Stable Diffusion to evaluate vision representations using matched rendered and photorealistic images.

paragraphs: DiffCut investigates whether a diffusion model's internal visual features can support image segmentation without supervised segmentation training. The task is to divide an image into meaningful regions. The authors focus on a diffusion UNet encoder and use only the features produced by its final self-attention block as the input to their segmentation method.

Those features feed a graph-based algorithm called recursive Normalized Cut. Repeated partitioning lets the method regulate how finely objects are separated, rather than committing to one undifferentiated grouping. The central combination is therefore a learned visual representation from a diffusion model and a graph-partitioning procedure that turns that representation into spatial regions.

The authors report significant improvements over previous state-of-the-art zero-shot segmentation methods, along with well-defined maps that capture intricate image details. These findings indicate that the selected diffusion features contain useful semantic information even when used outside image generation. They also support the possibility of using diffusion UNet encoders as foundation vision encoders for further downstream tasks.
neurips-2024-diffcut-catalyzing-zero-sho.tldr: DiffCut combines diffusion-encoder features with recursive graph partitioning to improve unsupervised zero-shot image segmentation.

paragraphs: Hierarchical clustering organizes data into nested groups, making the quality of an entire hierarchy the object of optimization. This paper proposes learning a probability distribution over hierarchies and optimizing the expected score under that distribution. The approach provides a probabilistic way to search for good hierarchical structures using gradient-based learning.

A key theoretical result concerns two objectives: Dasgupta cost and Tree-Sampling divergence. The authors prove that their expected formulations have the same globally optimal values as the corresponding discrete objectives. This preserves the optimum value for these scores, unlike some relaxed formulations. The result concerns the objectives' global optima; it does not itself establish that a training run reaches them.

The proposed Expected Probabilistic Hierarchies model uses differentiable hierarchy sampling for end-to-end optimization. An unbiased subgraph-sampling method enables scaling to large datasets. Evaluations include synthetic and real-world data in both vector and graph forms. EPH outperforms the compared approaches quantitatively, while qualitative assessments find meaningful hierarchical organization.
neurips-2024-expected-probabilistic-hier.tldr: EPH learns distributions over hierarchies using expected objectives that preserve the discrete global optimum values for two clustering scores.

paragraphs: XFADS learns hidden dynamical systems from observations using nonlinear Gaussian state-space models. The paper addresses a scalability tradeoff: simplifying either the dynamics or the inferred distribution over hidden states can make large problems manageable, but may weaken the model's ability to explain spatial and temporal structure or predict future observations.

The framework uses low-rank structure while retaining the ability to capture dense covariance, meaning statistical relationships across many hidden-state components. Its inference procedure combines sample-based approximate Gaussian message passing with low-rank updates predicted by an amortized inference model. Together, these operations approximately smooth hidden-state estimates across time, with time complexity that scales linearly in state dimensionality.

In comparisons with other deep state-space architectures, XFADS consistently learns more predictive generative models. Applied to physiological neural recordings, it forecasts population spiking and behavioral correlates from a small portion of individual trials. These results connect efficient uncertainty modeling with the practical aim of learning dynamics that can make useful forecasts.
neurips-2024-exponential-family-dynamica.tldr: XFADS uses structured approximate inference to learn predictive nonlinear state-space models with computation scaling linearly in hidden-state dimensionality.

paragraphs: Streamlined Inference targets the high computation and peak memory needed to generate videos with diffusion models. These demands become particularly restrictive for longer or higher-resolution outputs. The proposed framework changes how inference is executed without requiring training, using spatial and temporal properties already present in video diffusion models.

Two components work together to reduce memory. Feature Slicer divides input features into smaller pieces, and Operator Grouping processes each piece through a sequence of consecutive operators. The authors report that this reduces memory without sacrificing quality or speed. A third component, Step Rehash, uses similarities between neighboring diffusion steps to skip unnecessary steps and further accelerate generation.

Experiments show reductions in both peak memory and computational overhead, making high-quality video generation feasible on a single consumer GPU in the evaluated settings. One example reduces AnimateDiff's peak memory from 42 GB to 11 GB and achieves faster inference on a 2080 Ti. The contribution shows how reorganizing execution and exploiting repeated computation can improve deployment practicality.
neurips-2024-fast-and-memory-efficient-v.tldr: Streamlined Inference reduces video-diffusion memory and computation through feature partitioning, grouped operations, and selective step skipping without training.

paragraphs: AICT addresses high-resolution image harmonization by allowing color adjustments to vary locally across an image. The authors identify a weakness in approaches based on global adjustments or upsampled parameter maps: they can overlook local variation and leave parts of the result visually inconsistent. AICT instead predicts color transformations at the pixel level.

A parameter network generates multiple position-dependent three-dimensional lookup tables. These tables use both a pixel's color and its position to determine its transformation. To capture local nonlinear behavior, the method splits a color transformation into a cascade of sub-transformations using two lookup tables. This produces nonuniform sampling intervals, allowing the transformation to adjust its sampling adaptively.

The method also learns an image-level weight for each color transformation using global information. This connects detailed local adjustments to the overall appearance of the image, addressing harmony at both levels. Experiments report state-of-the-art performance with a lightweight architecture, supporting the combination of adaptive local color modeling and globally coordinated weighting.
neurips-2024-high-resolution-image-harmo.tldr: AICT combines position-dependent color lookup tables, adaptive sampling, and global weighting to improve high-resolution image harmonization.

paragraphs: This paper studies motion forecasting when an autonomous vehicle can use observations from other vehicles and roadside infrastructure. The authors argue that existing cooperative methods emphasize single-frame information to improve perception, leaving much of the observed motion history and interaction context underused. Their approach makes those trajectory-related features central to the shared representation.

The proposed V2X-Graph framework fuses trajectory features end to end for cooperative forecasting. It is designed to make that fusion interpretable while using motion and interaction information from cooperating devices. This changes the purpose of information sharing: cooperative observations contribute directly to forecasting representations, extending their role beyond improving what the vehicle perceives in one frame.

The authors evaluate vehicle-to-infrastructure forecasting on V2X-Seq. They also introduce V2X-Traj, described as the first real-world V2X motion-forecasting dataset, with multiple autonomous vehicles and infrastructure in every scenario. Experiments on both datasets show advantages for their method. Together, the framework and dataset support studying prediction with richer cooperation among traffic-observation sources.
neurips-2024-learning-cooperative-trajec.tldr: V2X-Graph uses shared motion and interaction histories for cooperative forecasting, supported by the new real-world V2X-Traj dataset.

paragraphs: This paper studies how a transformer begins solving tasks outside its pre-training collection using a controlled family of modular arithmetic problems. Each task computes ax + by modulo p, with the coefficient pair defining the task. Some coefficient pairs are used during pre-training, while the remaining tasks test out-of-distribution generalization.

The experiments show a transition as the number of pre-training tasks increases: the model moves from generalizing within its training distribution to succeeding on held-out tasks. In the studied setting, the smallest model capable of this broader generalization has two transformer blocks. For deeper models, the successful out-of-distribution phase is temporary, making early stopping necessary to retain it.

An interpretability analysis finds highly structured representations in both attention heads and multilayer perceptrons. The authors examine the algorithms those representations support and find that deeper models change algorithms as the number of in-context examples increases. The study links task diversity, model depth, and example availability to distinct learned behaviors within this arithmetic setting.
neurips-2024-learning-to-grok-emergence-.tldr: Controlled modular-arithmetic experiments reveal transitions in transformer generalization and algorithm choice as training-task diversity and in-context examples increase.

paragraphs: LION applies linear recurrent neural networks to 3D object detection in point clouds. Its motivation is the quadratic computation associated with transformer-based long-range interactions. By running linear RNNs over grouped features within a window-based framework, LION allows feature interaction across much larger groups than the transformer-based methods discussed in the paper.

Sparse 3D data creates a spatial-modeling challenge for this approach. LION introduces a 3D spatial feature descriptor into the recurrent operators to strengthen their handling of spatial information. It also generates 3D voxels to densify foreground features, drawing on the autoregressive nature of the recurrent models. These additions address geometry and sparsity alongside the computational benefit of larger groups.

Experiments support the proposed components and demonstrate the framework with Mamba, RWKV, and RetNet operators. LION-Mamba achieves reported state-of-the-art results on Waymo, nuScenes, Argoverse V2, and ONCE. The framework also supports several advanced linear RNN operators on KITTI, showing that the design can accommodate multiple recurrent architectures.
neurips-2024-lion-linear-group-rnn-for-3.tldr: LION combines linear recurrent feature interaction with spatial descriptors and voxel generation for accurate detection in sparse 3D point clouds.

paragraphs: MultiPull reconstructs continuous surfaces from raw 3D point clouds. The paper focuses on the loss of local detail when neural methods learn signed distance functions without ground-truth distances or surface normals. These functions represent a surface through a spatial field, but overly smooth learned fields can erase the fine structure needed for accurate reconstruction.

The method learns implicit fields at multiple scales and optimizes the signed distance function from coarse to fine. It maps 3D query points into frequency features so that different levels of detail are available during optimization. This provides a way to connect broad surface structure with finer geometric information during the same reconstruction process.

MultiPull also introduces constraints based on spatial distance and normal consistency. These guide the multiscale optimization toward geometrically consistent surfaces while supporting detail recovery. Experiments on commonly used object and scene benchmarks report better surface reconstruction than state-of-the-art methods. The findings support combining multilevel representations with geometric constraints to improve reconstruction from raw points.
neurips-2024-multipull-detailing-signed-.tldr: MultiPull improves surface reconstruction from raw point clouds through coarse-to-fine implicit fields and geometric consistency constraints.

paragraphs: This paper examines how to train latent diffusion models more efficiently while improving image-generation performance. Large-scale end-to-end training is computationally expensive, which restricts research toward fine-tuning existing models or smaller experiments. The authors study design choices intended to make scaling to larger datasets and higher image resolutions more practical.

Their first focus is conditioning: how the model receives semantic information, such as a text prompt or class name, alongside low-level information, such as crop size or random flipping. They propose a mechanism that separates these two kinds of conditioning. This treats the image's requested meaning and its low-level processing information as distinct inputs within the conditioning design.

Their second focus is transferring representations learned on smaller, lower-resolution datasets to larger training settings. A systematic experimental study examines both conditioning and pre-training strategies. The paper reports state-of-the-art text-to-image performance on CC12M at 512 resolution. Its contribution combines an architectural change with evidence about training strategy, targeting performance and training efficiency together.
neurips-2024-on-improved-conditioning-me.tldr: The paper studies diffusion pre-training and separates semantic from low-level conditioning, reporting state-of-the-art CC12M results at 512 resolution.

paragraphs: AdaptIR addresses how a pre-trained image-restoration model can adapt to different kinds of degradation while updating few parameters. The authors identify high computational cost and limited generalization to unseen degradations as problems for existing all-in-one restoration models. They investigate parameter-efficient transfer as an alternative, while arguing that homogeneous representations restrict existing adaptation methods.

Their solution is a mixture of experts with an orthogonal multibranch design. Different branches capture local spatial, global spatial, and channel representations. An adaptive combination mechanism then brings these representation bases together for different degradations. The architecture is intended to supply varied types of features within a compact adaptation mechanism.

Experiments report stable performance on tasks involving a single degradation and strong results on tasks combining degradations. The reported setup trains only 0.6% of parameters for eight hours. These findings support the value of heterogeneous representations when adapting restoration models: a small trainable component can draw on several complementary forms of image information.
neurips-2024-parameter-efficient-adaptat.tldr: AdaptIR adapts restoration models through complementary expert branches, reporting strong hybrid-degradation results while training only 0.6% of parameters.

paragraphs: This paper investigates whether random-noise pre-training can prepare a neural network for later learning. Inspired by spontaneous neural activity, the authors study networks trained with feedback alignment, an approach that teaches through backward feedback without weight transport. The biological motivation frames the question, while the reported findings concern the studied learning algorithm.

Noise pre-training changes forward weights so they align with backward feedback, preparing the network to use teaching errors. The resulting networks learn faster and reach higher accuracy than networks without this preparation, with performance reported as comparable to backpropagation. The authors also find that noise pre-training lowers the effective dimensionality of the weights.

That reduced dimensionality acts as pre-regularization: subsequent training learns simpler, low-rank solutions with lower generalization error. The study also reports robust generalization to a novel out-of-distribution dataset and reduced meta-loss, indicating improved adaptation across tasks. Together, the results suggest that noise can serve as useful preparation for feedback-alignment learning before task-specific training begins.
neurips-2024-pretraining-with-random-noi.tldr: Random-noise pre-training improves feedback-alignment learning by aligning forward weights with feedback and encouraging simpler subsequent solutions.

paragraphs: This paper develops self-supervised image denoising using only noisy images captured in a single shot. It revisits the blind-spot approach through transformers, emphasizing their ability to connect pixels over long distances. The authors identify dependence between noise in related pixels as an important obstacle to strong blind-spot denoising performance.

The proposed directional self-attention module restricts attention using a half-plane grid, creating the model's blind-spot structure. That restriction shapes which image information can interact, but also affects performance by narrowing the attention pattern. A Siamese architecture with mutual learning is introduced to mitigate those effects, pairing the attention constraint with a mechanism for improving learning.

Benchmark experiments show better performance than existing self-supervised and clean-image-free denoising methods. The findings support combining long-range transformer interactions with deliberately constrained attention and mutual learning. The contribution is a coordinated architecture for learning from noisy observations, with each component addressing a different aspect of making blind-spot denoising work on real-world images.
neurips-2024-pseudo-siamese-blind-spot-t.tldr: Directional attention and Siamese mutual learning improve blind-spot transformer denoising using only single-shot noisy images.

paragraphs: This paper studies depth estimation from multiple views with a model designed to behave consistently across 3D reference frames. Earlier methods embed geometric inputs such as rays, but often lack equivariance or approximate it through data augmentation. Equivariance makes the representation respond systematically when the coordinate frame changes, providing a structural prior for 3D learning.

The authors incorporate SE(3) equivariance into Perceiver IO. Their design uses spherical harmonics for positional encoding to ensure rotation equivariance, together with specialized equivariant encoder and decoder components. This places the desired geometric behavior inside the architecture, addressing inconsistencies that can arise when it is learned only approximately from augmented data.

The model is evaluated on stereo depth estimation and achieves reported state-of-the-art results on real-world datasets without explicit geometric constraints or extensive data augmentation. These findings support architectural equivariance as a useful bias for multi-view depth learning. The contribution connects a specific symmetry-aware representation design to improved depth-estimation performance in the evaluated setting.
neurips-2024-se-3-equivariant-ray-embedd.tldr: An equivariant Perceiver IO architecture improves stereo depth estimation by building consistent 3D reference-frame behavior into its representations.

paragraphs: SHiRA addresses a deployment tradeoff in adapting large models. Fusing a LoRA adapter into a base model avoids inference overhead, but rapid switching becomes harder. Keeping it separate permits switching while adding latency. The paper also targets concept loss when several adapters are combined, where their learned concepts are less well preserved together.

SHiRA directly tunes only 1–2% of base-model weights, producing a sparse adapter that can be switched in fused mode without inference overhead. The authors provide theoretical and empirical insights into how sparsity can reduce concept loss during multi-adapter fusion. This ties the adaptation structure to both switching efficiency and the preservation of multiple concepts.

Experiments on large vision and language models report significant improvements over LoRA. A PEFT-library implementation trains at nearly LoRA's speed while using up to 16% less peak GPU memory. Loading SHiRA onto a base model is reported as 5–16 times faster than LoRA fusion on a CPU, demonstrating a practical switching benefit.
neurips-2024-sparse-high-rank-adapters-b.tldr: SHiRA tunes sparse subsets of model weights to enable fast fused-adapter switching and reduce concept loss when adapters are combined.

paragraphs: Model-GLUE studies how to build a stronger language-model system from a diverse collection of existing models. Combining models can reduce performance when their structures or starting points differ. The paper therefore treats selection and aggregation as connected decisions, asking how techniques such as merging and model mixtures can work together across a heterogeneous collection.

The authors first benchmark existing scaling approaches, particularly selective merging and mixture variants. They use those results to construct a strategy that groups models suitable for merging, chooses a merging method, and combines the resulting clusters through a model-level mixture. This staged process accounts for compatibility within groups while retaining a way to aggregate across groups.

Experiments on a diverse Llama-2-based model collection report an average performance improvement of 5.61% without additional training. The result supports the proposed selection-and-aggregation guideline in that evaluated collection. Its practical contribution is a coordinated way to reuse available models, turning benchmarking insights into decisions about which models to combine and how.
neurips-2024-texttt-model-glue-democrati.tldr: Model-GLUE combines compatibility-based model merging with model-level mixtures, reporting a 5.61% average improvement without additional training.

paragraphs: This paper addresses the detection of harmful memes on the Chinese Internet, where the authors identify a shortage of reliable datasets and effective detectors. They introduce ToxiCN MM, described as the first Chinese harmful-meme dataset. It contains 12,000 samples with fine-grained annotations for meme types, providing organized material for studying this detection problem.

The paper also proposes Multimodal Knowledge Enhancement, or MKE, as a baseline detector. MKE incorporates contextual information from meme content to improve the model's understanding of Chinese memes. The method makes context part of the detection approach, connecting the interpretation of a meme's content to the decision about whether it is harmful.

The evaluation combines quantitative experiments with qualitative analysis across multiple baselines, including large language models and MKE. Results show that the task remains challenging for existing models while supporting MKE's effectiveness. The dataset and detector contribute complementary resources: one establishes a basis for examining the problem, and the other tests a context-enhanced approach to solving it.
neurips-2024-towards-comprehensive-detec.tldr: The paper introduces a 12,000-sample Chinese harmful-meme dataset and a context-enhanced detector that proves effective on a challenging task.

paragraphs: This paper studies how transformers can process long videos more efficiently by merging their tokens. Sampling the input or dropping tokens may discard information, motivating ways to combine representations. The authors argue that similarity alone is insufficient for deciding which video tokens to merge: their saliency, or importance, should also influence the decision.

The study explores a progression of strategies, beginning with an extension of image token merging and then considering merging concentrated within regions. It culminates in a learnable Video Token Merging algorithm that dynamically uses saliency. The central design choice is to make token reduction sensitive to which parts of the video matter, alongside the relationships among token representations.

Experiments on long-form video classification show better or comparable performance on LVU, COIN, and Breakfast. Relative to baseline algorithms, the approach reduces memory costs by 84% and increases throughput by approximately 6.89 times. These results support saliency-aware merging as a practical way to reduce the cost of long-video processing.
neurips-2024-video-token-merging-for-lon.tldr: Learnable saliency-aware video token merging maintains or improves classification performance while sharply reducing memory costs and increasing throughput.

paragraphs: This paper studies 3D perception using an event camera and a conventional frame-based camera viewing a scene from different positions. Such systems can help in dynamic or challenging environments, but limited event datasets can lead to overfitting and weak generalization. The proposed framework draws on models pre-trained with diverse image datasets to address that shortage.

A visual-prompting technique aligns the representations of events and frames, allowing an off-the-shelf stereo-matching model to operate without additional training. The framework also uses a pre-trained monocular depth model. Its depth information guides a disparity-refinement module, helping improve robustness in both static and moving parts of a scene.

Experiments on real-world datasets report stronger zero-shot performance and improved generalization compared with existing approaches. The contribution is a way to connect event-based observations with image-domain models through representation alignment and depth-guided refinement. The findings support transferring existing image-model capabilities into this mixed-sensor setting without training a new stereo model for the event domain.
neurips-2024-zero-shot-event-intensity-a.tldr: Visual prompting and monocular depth cues enable pre-trained image models to perform event–frame stereo estimation without additional training.
